issues.description: The problem statement (both the UML and textual description) describe SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery as taking four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) / signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String, String, int, int), but the template's example call and the solution implement acceptSupplyDelivery with three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity) / signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int). This mismatch between the specification and the provided/template/solution code can confuse students about the correct method signature to implement and may cause tests or examples to fail.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the acceptSupplyDelivery signature consistent across artifacts. Either (A) update the problem statement UML and textual description to specify the three-parameter signature acceptSupplyDelivery(String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) (and remove the unused supplier name), or (B) change the template example and the solution to include the supplier name parameter so the signature matches the UML (acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity)). Prefer option A if the supplier name is not used functionally, to match the current template and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies acceptSupplyDelivery as taking four parameters (supplier name, ingredient name, price, quantity) but the solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery with only three parameters (ingredient name, price, quantity). This mismatch in the method signature for the same conceptual operation (accepting a supply delivery) can confuse students: the UML and textual description indicate a supplier parameter that is missing in the provided implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signatures consistent. Either update the problem statement to require acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (removing the supplier parameter) or modify the implementation to match the spec: change the method to acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and handle or document the supplier parameter (it can be stored, logged, or ignored) so the solution matches the UML/textual description.
